query: For the paper "How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?" (arXiv: 1906.01502), answer this question: What languages do they experiment with?

drafts: The experiments cover several language sets: POS tagging is performed using Universal Dependencies data for 41 languages [1], with the 41-language list given in a footnote [14]. NER experiments use two datasets: the publicly available CoNLL-2002 and -2003 sets, containing Dutch, Spanish, English, and German, and an in-house dataset with 16 languages using the same CoNLL categories [12]; the 16 languages of the in-house dataset are listed in a footnote as Arabic, Bengali, Czech, German, English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, and Chinese [13].

cited_sources.text: 2.2 Part of speech tagging experiments We perform POS experiments using Universal De- pendencies (UD) (Nivre et al., 2016) data for 41 languages.3 We use the evaluation sets from Ze- man et al. Table 2 shows M-BERT zero- shot results for four European languages. We see that M-BERT generalizes well across languages, achieving over 80% accuracy for all pairs.
